content_metadata.description: An educational video that explains the various aspects of the cardiovascular system, including its components, functions, and blood flow dynamics.

qAndA.answer: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs, while the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the heart.
qAndA.question: What is the difference between the pulmonary artery and the pulmonary vein?

qAndA.answer: The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it has to pump oxygenated blood with enough force to reach all the cells in the body.
qAndA.question: Which ventricle of the heart has the thickest wall? Why?

qAndA.answer: The septum is a barrier that separates the left and right sides of the heart. This prevents the mixing of deoxygenated blood (on the right side) and oxygenated blood (on the left side).
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of the septum in the heart?

qAndA.answer: Deoxygenated blood from the body travels to the right atrium of the heart via the vena cava. It then moves to the right ventricle and is pumped to the lungs via the pulmonary artery. In the lungs, the blood is oxygenated. The oxygenated blood returns to the heart's left atrium through the pulmonary vein, then goes to the left ventricle and is pumped to the body through the aorta.
qAndA.question: Describe the flow of blood from the body back to the body, highlighting the role of the lungs.
